newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end down as C-C Amatil slips.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end down as C-C Amatil slips.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2398 -15 US 30yr cl 6.46 +0.04
*Stocks ended down slightly with a slide in C-C Amatil stock weighing on the market. Volume 419.5 million shares, value A$706.2 million, 1,084 stocks traded, 313 steady, 414 up, 357 down.
Australian shares closed slightly weaker on Monday with opening gains eradicated by afternoon profit-taking after the market was held back by a sell-off of Coca-Cola Amatil stock.
Key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index closed 3.5 points lower at 2,383.8, after setting an intra-day and all-time high level of 2,398.6 during early morning trade.
The December share price index ended down 15 points at 2,398 and at an 14.2 point premium to the underlying index.
Trading was active as engineering group ANI topped turnover after major shareholder Ross Palmer sold 40 million shares.

"The market was doing alright even with the slump in Coca-Coal Amatil stock this morning but this afternoon investors took the top off the market across the board," said Eric Gale, director of institutions at Sydney broker, Ord Minnett.
Gale said the late sell-down could be attributed to profit-taking after the market's strong rise in the past two session in the past week.
"The market expected Coca-Cola to get slammed, and that's exactly what happened," Gale said.
Coca-Cola Amatil disappointed investors late on Friday when it warned that its 1996 profit would be flat.
Dealers said that because the market had the weekend to digest Coca-Cola Amatil's profit downgrade, it was possible the company's shares could make a slight recovery within the next two sessions.

Major banks were the most noticeable targets of profit-taking with the National Australia Bank and Commonwealth Bank losing all their early gains, while resource majors BHP and CRA ended firmer but off the day's highs.
Behind the strength of the resources sector was the more robust outlook for base metal prices, after copper found good support in active trade on the London Metal Excahnge on Friday.
In other markets, Australian bonds underperformed its dollar bloc partners as the local market made space for fresh supply.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds finished at 7.16 percent, up 0.09 percentage points from Friday's closing level.
The Australian dollar held to a tight orbit around 79 US cents, the market starved for domestic news.
At 5.00 p.m (0600 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7909/14.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade remained buoyant however futures business eased today with the market's fortunes.
Total options traded 53,272 (48,719)
